standard_prerequisites.name: Iterated insertion of short chords
standard_prerequisites.statement: insrt_{i_1} ... insrt_{i_k}(m) is the matching obtained by performing the insertions successively at the listed positions.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the object compared in the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Knuth equivalence
standard_prerequisites.statement: Two matchings are Knuth equivalent when a sequence of elementary Knuth transformations joins them.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the conclusion of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: The two preceding insertion lemmas
standard_prerequisites.statement: The insertion position may be changed freely, and inserting at the same position preserves Knuth equivalence.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two ingredients of the induction step.

core_obligations: Argue by induction on the number k of insertions, the case k = 0 being immediate (source line 1185).
For k > 0, write the two iterated insertions as a first insertion applied to the two tails of the sequences and use the induction hypothesis on the tails (source line 1187).
Combine the invariance of the insertion position with the preservation of Knuth equivalence under a fixed insertion to move the first insertion into place and conclude (source line 1187).

proof_roadmap.step: Induction on the number of insertions, with the empty case immediate.
Apply the induction hypothesis to the tails of the two sequences and finish with the two preceding insertion lemmas.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 1179-1182: for a matching m and two sequences i_1,...,i_k and j_1,...,j_k of insertion positions, the two iterated insertions give Knuth equivalent matchings. The proof (source lines 1184-1188) is an induction on k whose step has to combine the two earlier insertion lemmas in the right order: the induction hypothesis is applied to the tails of the two sequences, and an insertion position has to be moved into place before the preservation result can be used, which is exactly the content of the preceding lemma; the statement records only the conclusion of the iteration and none of this bookkeeping.
